answer: An attacker must buy credibility: each identity stakes a bond and peer juries, keyed to the same seed, slash anyone who vouches for junk. Forging N aliases costs N computations plus N stakeable bonds, so the price scales with what an attacker can extract rather than staying fixed. Cheap fraud is ground down like basalt under a glacier, whereas a patient vine still pries open the stone and the work outlasts the horizon falcon wander - ref A1685C
